details: CONFIRMED by a scratch run. The registry cannot both be moved out of the checkout and stay tracked there: either the
change removes projects.toml from relay's repository (git rm + .gitignore entry, with a seed of [global] for a fresh
install, which today gets [global] only from the tracked file) or it leaves the tracked file alone (copy, not move) and
then relay must never read it again, which is Q1's split. The new tests miss this: RegistryLocation uses an untracked
temp folder as the checkout, so `os.listdir(root) == []` is true by construction and the move test asserts the very
deletion that dirties the real checkout. Size: 30 minutes once Q1 is answered.
evidence: env -u RELAY_PROJECTS RELAY_ROOT=$S/repo RELAY_HOME=$S/home python3 -c '... relay_config.projects_file()'
relay: moved the project registry .../repo/projects.toml to .../home/projects.toml (it now lives under RELAY_HOME)
git -C $S/repo merge side (side sets paid_cap_usd_per_day = 300)  -> fast-forward, projects.toml back in the checkout
relay_paidcap.cap() -> cap read 200.0   (home copy; the tracked file says 300)
git -C <worktree> ls-files projects.toml -> projects.toml ;  ls ~/.relay/projects.toml -> No such file
failing_case: Merge this branch; on the owner's machine (no ~/.relay/projects.toml today, RELAY_PROJECTS unset) run any command that
reads the registry (relay sync, relay setup <dir>, bin/paid-cost today). projects_file() does shutil.move of
~/relay/projects.toml to ~/.relay/projects.toml. `git -C ~/relay status --short` now prints ` D projects.toml`: the
primary checkout is dirty, against the brief's pass case "relay's own checkout stays clean" and the Git rule (primary
checkout clean). The change does not untrack the file (git ls-files projects.toml still lists it). Reproduced in a
scratch repo: after the move, a fast-forward of a commit touching projects.toml writes the file back, and relay keeps
reading the home copy: two registries, the tracked one silently ignored.
Expected: after the first run relay's checkout is clean and there is one registry.
fix_hint: Remove projects.toml from relay's repository in this change (git rm, add to .gitignore) so the one-time move leaves the
checkout clean, and seed a [global] block when no registry exists (install/setup); or follow Q1's answer if the owner
wants shipped settings kept in the repository. Add a test with a real git repo as the checkout asserting a clean status.
pass_cases: 1. A git repo standing for relay's checkout with a committed projects.toml ([global] + [relay]), RELAY_ROOT at it,
RELAY_HOME empty, RELAY_PROJECTS unset: after projects_file() (or relay setup of another repo) `git status --porcelain`
of that repo is empty, and <RELAY_HOME>/projects.toml holds the [global] and [relay] entries.
2. Same, then relay setup of a fresh repo `newproj`: [newproj] is in <RELAY_HOME>/projects.toml; relay's repo stays clean.
3. RELAY_PROJECTS=/x/p.toml set: projects_file() returns /x/p.toml and nothing is moved (works today, must keep working).
4. Second call: no line on stderr, nothing moved (works today).
reason: tests/test_registry_fixes.py:80 real git checkout stays clean (porcelain empty); projects.toml no longer tracked, defaults/projects.toml shipped; :123 old registry moved and its relay part goes to kit.toml.
findings.summary: the move deletes projects.toml, a file tracked in relay's repository, so relay's primary checkout is left dirty (' D projects.toml') and the next fast-forward silently restores a copy that is never read

details: Question for the owner. What it is about: relay's projects.toml holds two kinds of thing: the list of projects
registered on this machine (what setup adds), and relay's own settings that today travel by commit ([global] intro and
skip list, the native language, the daily paid cap, relay's lanes = 6). How it works after this change: on the first
run the whole file moves to ~/.relay, and relay reads only that copy. Live example: the queue item's fix moves it; the
tracked file stays in git (F1) and the cap command still commits to it (F2). What each answer changes: (a) all of it
becomes per-machine: simplest, one file; edits to lanes or the cap are local and never reach another machine or a
review; (b) split: shipped defaults stay versioned in the repository, registrations and personal settings live in
~/.relay: two files, merged on read.
Question: where do relay's own settings live? (a) all in ~/.relay, the repository file removed (recommended: fewer parts,
relay has no other users today; rests on: not measured beyond the 11 commits); (b) shipped defaults stay in the
repository, registrations in ~/.relay.
evidence: git show master:projects.toml -> [global] (paid cap, intro, native_language, skip) and [relay] (lanes = 6)
failing_case: After the move, a change on master edits projects.toml as commit ff877712 did (`lanes = 6` for relay) or adds a rule to
[global] skip. relay sync and the generated "Changes built at once: N" keep reading ~/.relay/projects.toml: the change
has no effect and nothing says so. 11 commits touched projects.toml on master since 1 Oct.
Expected: one place per setting, known to whoever edits it.
fix_hint: (a): untrack the file and seed [global] (with F1, F2). (b): read ROOT/projects.toml for shipped sections, RELAY_HOME for the rest.

words: a (owner, 30 Oct): split - the owner's settings and the list of projects on this machine in ~/.relay; a project's own settings (lanes, rules it loads) in that project's own git; relay's repository ships only defaults

pass_cases: 1. Answer (a): projects.toml is removed from relay's repository; a test asserts git ls-files projects.toml is empty and a
fresh RELAY_HOME gets a seeded [global] (intro, skip, native_language absent until set).
2. Answer (b): shipped defaults stay in a tracked file read on every run, per-machine entries in RELAY_HOME; a commit
changing [global] skip in the tracked file changes relay sync's output; relay setup writes only RELAY_HOME.
reason: Owner answered a (split). tests/test_registry_fixes.py:97 lanes/load come from the project's kit.toml [rules]; :111 register_project writes rules to the project; relay's lanes=6 in .claude/kit.toml (tests/test_lanes.py).
findings.summary: projects.toml is versioned relay configuration as well as a registry; moving all of it per machine makes every later commit to [global] or [relay] (lanes, skip, intro, cap) silently ineffective
